newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rock star Danko held for drug smuggling in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Rock star Danko held for drug smuggling in Japan.

text.p: Canadian rock legend Rick Danko has been arrested on drug smuggling charges while on a tour in Japan and will soon go on trial, a police spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman for police in Chiba, a large outer Tokyo suburb, told Reuters that Danko was arrested on May 6 during a raid on his hotel room.
He said police found 1.25 grams (less than an ounce) of heroin hidden in a magazine mailed to him from the United States.
Since the raid, Danko has been in custody at a police detention centre in Chiba. The Chiba District Court has not set an opening date yet for his trial.
Danko, a bass guitarist and lead singer for the famed group The Band, which broke up in 1976, was on a five-concert tour of Japan which started on April 30 and ended on May 6.
The last concert on May 6 in Tokyo went ahead without him after his arrest. Organisers at the time said Danko's failure to appear in the last concert was because of illness.

Prosecutors charged Danko on May 23 with violating the Narcotics Control Law and the Customs Law, the spokesman said. If found guilty, Danko could be sentenced to a maximum three years in prison but could also be deported.
Danko was scheduled to release a live album based on the Japan concerts, his first since his last solo album in 1978.

The Band, known for hits such as "The Weight", "The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down" and "Up on Cripple Creek", broke up in 1976 with the star-studded "Last Waltz" concert which was also made into a hit film.
The group first came to prominence as a back-up band for rock star Bob Dylan.
They went on to become one of the most successful and highly regarded rock groups of the past three decades.

Japan's most famous drug arrest of a rock star was the early 1980s detention of Paul McCartney who was nabbed for smuggling marijuana into the country. He spent nine days in a jail before he was deported.
Japan's strict anti-drugs law had long kept The Rolling Stones from touring the country because of guitarist Keith Richards' past drug conviction.
The members were issued visas for the first time in 1990 for the "Steel Wheels" tour.
